I've been reading "Stranger Than We Can Imagine: Making Sense of the Twentieth Century" by John Higgs and it is quite good.

I pretty much read only non fiction, I like facts and seeing how the world truly is, don't really care about made up stories with subjective feelings and descriptions. Sometimes I do read some fiction but it's maybe 10% of my reading material.

Right now I'm getting into geopolitics.

  • Revenge of geography - Robert D. Kaplan - great book about how geography affects the destiny of countries and nations, I've seen tons of recommendations of Kaplan's books in geopolitical forums and I chose this one and wasn't disappointing.

  • Flashpoints - George Friedman - describes potential areas of conflict in Europe, sort of a pessimistic view of what would happen if for example the EU failed and Russia got more aggressive, both of which are very real possibilities with some other potential events. Thrilling analysis.

From history

  • 1491: New Revelations of the Americas Before Columbus - Charles C. Mann - great look into precolumbian native American societies, explains why they were so backward compared to Europe and yet shows that some of their perceived backwardness was due to complete collapse after their discovery due to disease and conflict.

Society

  • In Praise of Slow - Carl Honoré - a book showing how society is too fast and that we need to chill out, one of my personal favorites.

  • Omnivore's Dilemma - Michael Pollan - great book about the three main ways to get food i.e. industrial production bought in the supermarket, organic and hunting/gathering. It starts of great and then the author tries to be sort of poetic/emotional and at parts it's sort of drivel but the the bulk of the book is great.

I have lots more, these were just some recent ones that came to mind.

Nonfiction is all I can really get into anymore, I love the genre. My picks:
